clauses.Clocks: *1.1.0* T and K only: the submission was made by T (`submitted_at` <= T) and is known by K; the decision's `effective_at` <= T and its `received_at` <= K. Completion and due times are not used (M04 and M07 use them)

clauses.Exclusions: none from C. `C_unresolved` (submeasure) is shown separately and is in neither numerator nor denominator
clauses.Label: "source-evidenced accepted completed-leg coverage". It is evidenced coverage, not an estimate of unseen business outcomes. Client assertions never count
clauses.Limits: *1.1.0* evidenced coverage, never prevalence or an estimate of unseen outcomes; a leg whose unit is covered by more than one incompatible family is `conflicted`, not covered. Replacement, void and retraction lineage (`src/cci/coverage.py`) is exercised by the public goldens only; none occurs in the v1 bulk population
clauses.Milestone: *1.1.0* the final encounter decision (stage `encounter_decision`) for each U unit of the leg, bound to that unit's submission. Transport and syntax receipts are not the milestone
clauses.Numerator: legs every one of whose U units has current qualifying acceptance: a final encounter decision `accepted`, basis `originating` or `forwarded_originating`, effective by T, received by K, bound to the unit's exact scoped submission, with no incompatible decision

clauses.Clocks: *1.1.0* as M01 (submission by T and known by K; decision `effective_at` <= T and `received_at` <= K); `missing_claim` uses claim version `available_at` <= T

clauses.Exclusions: *1.1.0* legs counted in the M01 numerator, which are not uncovered. `C_unresolved` legs are outside C and are an M01 submeasure. Counts at line, response or attempt grain are not part of this partition
clauses.Limits: *1.1.0* a leg is counted once, under the first state in the order above that it meets, so a state's count is not the number of legs with that condition
clauses.Lineage: *1.1.0* `src/cci/evidence.py` `resolve` (leg state assignment over unit outcomes, `leg-coverage.json`) via `src/cci/cells.py`
clauses.Milestone: *1.1.0* as M01, the final encounter decision per U unit; `missing_claim` is decided by the unit's initial-preparation readiness at T and `not_submitted` by the absence of a submission made by T
clauses.Numerator: *1.1.0* not a ratio: `uncovered` is C minus the M01 numerator, partitioned into the nine mutually exclusive states above; each state is a count of legs
clauses.Owner role: *1.1.0* encounter reporting operations (the M01 owner; M02 partitions the complement of the M01 numerator)
clauses.Population: C. Mutually exclusive states, *1.0.1* assigned in this order over the leg's U units: `conflicted` (any unit conflicted), `missing_claim` (any unit missing construction), `not_submitted` (any unit with no submission by T), `voided` (every unit accepted or voided, at least one voided), `rejected` (any unit with a source-evidenced rejection), `partial_required_components` (some units accepted, none rejected), `client_asserted_only` (any unit whose only evidence is a record-specific client assertion), `no_evidence` (every unit's evidence basis is `no_usable_evidence`), `unresolved` (the rest, including legs whose only context is an aggregate note). A rejected component explains the leg before a partial acceptance does. `uncovered` = C minus M01 numerator; the states sum to `uncovered`

clauses.Limits: *1.1.0* FULL period only. Acceptance requires every required component. A different population from M01 and M16, never presented as one funnel with them
clauses.Milestone: *1.1.0* the first business submission made by T (fixes the cohort) and the final encounter decision on that attempt; a source-evidenced terminal syntax rejection at component, record, batch or transaction grain is a terminal prerequisite rejection of the attempt

clauses.Clocks: *1.1.0* census `completed_at` (the unit trigger), `acceptance_due_at`, T (deadline <= T; decision `effective_at` <= T and at or before the unit's deadline) and K (decision `received_at` <= K)
clauses.Exclusions: *1.1.0* `partly_due`, `not_yet_due` and `timing_undetermined` legs are outside the denominator and published separately; `C_unresolved` legs are outside C

M04.title: Coverage at each component's own deadline

clauses.Clocks: *1.1.0* delivery `submitted_at` (trigger, <= T and <= K); due time = trigger + the stage's hours (follow-up + 120 h); receipt `received_at` <= T and <= K for the state at T, and `received_at` in (T, K] for `later_resolution`. A receipt at the due instant is on time; an obligation is overdue only when T is strictly after its due time. `effective_at` is not used for timeliness
clauses.Denominator: *1.1.0* not a ratio: `expected_timed_receipts` (receipt obligations with a due time) is the partitioned total, overall and per stage
clauses.Exclusions: *1.1.0* untimed obligations (`no_return_promise`, `not_established`) and follow-up obligations are outside `expected_timed_receipts` and counted separately; a delivery made after T, or not known by K, creates no obligation
clauses.Limits: *1.1.0* FULL only. Response outcome is M16, not this measure. Every v1 receipt rule is the pinned contract's elapsed window; the calendar-rule, conditional-final and transaction-result paths in `src/cci/evidence.py` are used by no v1 policy
clauses.Milestone: *1.1.0* the first delivery of the business attempt (the trigger) and each expected response stage: transport receipt, syntax acknowledgment, encounter decision; the follow-up obligation runs from submission
clauses.Numerator: *1.1.0* not a ratio: timed receipt obligations are counted by state, and the states partition `expected_timed_receipts`; no single on-time rate is defined
clauses.Population: receipt obligations of S deliveries whose policy stage expectation is `expected`. Due: transport 1 h, syntax 4 h, encounter decision 72 h from first delivery
clauses.States: `satisfied_on_time` (first receipt received by T and K at or before due), `satisfied_late`, `pending` (none yet and T at or before due), `overdue` (none and T after due), `justifiably_cancelled` (a terminal syntax rejection cancels the final decision obligation). Timeliness uses received time only; a restated business acceptance never backdates receipt. `later_resolution` counts obligations unresolved at T with a receipt in (T, K]
clauses.Untimed: : `no_return_promise` (route structurally unavailable) and `not_established` create no receipt promise. *1.0.1:* they are counted once per delivery at the final-decision stage, where the business outcome would arrive; a non-final stage that is not established creates no obligation row. Follow-up obligations (120 h, SYN-C04 to SYN-C06) are separate. Per-stage and follow-up states include `justifiably_cancelled`

clauses.Age: a preparation item ages from its onset (the later of its trigger and its claim version's availability) against its governed stage deadline (initial 24 h, submission 48 h); an overdue receipt or follow-up ages from its contractual due time; a rejection ages from its observed onset (earliest received rejecting evidence) with no deadline established
clauses.Clocks: *1.1.0* T (open at T; `governed_overdue` when T is strictly after the due time), K (obligations and rejections use evidence received by K), the unit trigger (completion, or the documented cancellation's `effective_at`), claim version `available_at`, `preparation_due_at` (trigger + 24 h), `reporting_due_at` (trigger + 48 h), receipt and follow-up due times, and the `received_at` of the earliest rejecting evidence
clauses.Denominator: *1.1.0* not a ratio; no rate is computed
clauses.Exclusions: *1.1.0* a condition that is not open and actionable at T creates no item: a receipt or follow-up obligation that is satisfied, pending or justifiably cancelled, a ready readiness row, a U unit whose outcome is not `rejected`. Closing an item changes no claim, financial or coverage fact
clauses.Limits: *1.1.0* FULL only. A rejection item carries no SLA conclusion. `<kind>:median_age_hours` uses the shared nearest-rank rule over items with a known age. Owner roles are synthetic role names, not people
clauses.Lineage: *1.1.0* `src/cci/workitems.py` (`build`, `attach_rejection_onsets`; `work-items.jsonl`) over readiness rows from `src/cci/claims.py` `readiness` and obligations and unit outcomes from `src/cci/evidence.py` `resolve`, via `src/cci/cells.py`
clauses.Milestone: *1.1.0* T: an item is open when its condition holds at T. The governing event is the governed stage deadline for a preparation item, the obligation's contractual due time for a receipt or follow-up item, and the source-evidenced rejection for a rejection item
clauses.Numerator: *1.1.0* not a ratio: a count of open work items at T, by kind, with their ages
clauses.Owner role: *1.1.0 (label made singular; per kind added)* claims operations (`preparation_blocked`, `preparation_conflict`), encounter operations (`receipt_overdue`, `encounter_rejection`), client operations (`follow_up_overdue`)
clauses.Population: work items at T: `preparation_blocked` and `preparation_conflict` (one per blocked or conflicting readiness row at encounter, audit or initial stage), `receipt_overdue`, `follow_up_overdue`, `encounter_rejection` (*1.0.1:* one per rejected U unit, because the correction decision is taken per component and target)

other: *1.0.1:* `timing_undetermined` counts items whose timing basis is `not_established` (no deadline exists for them: every rejection item), whether or not their onset is known.
M06.title: Open actionable issues and their age

clauses.Denominator: *1.1.0* not a ratio; no rate is computed

clauses.Milestone: *1.1.0* response receipt: each raw row's binding, at the position, to an actual submission made by T

clauses.Numerator: *1.1.0* not a ratio: a status record (last attempted and last successful run, outcome, expected next run, observer time, expiry, stale or unknown status)

clauses.Exclusions: *1.1.0* none from U: a unit with no submission is `unresolved` with basis `no_usable_evidence`, and a unit on a structurally unavailable return route remains a reporting requirement
clauses.Limits: *1.1.0* absence of evidence is neither acceptance nor rejection. A different population from M01 and M03, never one funnel with them
clauses.Milestone: *1.1.0* the final encounter decision per unit; the return expectation is the evidence policy's encounter-decision stage expectation
clauses.Numerator: *1.1.0* `source_evidenced_outcomes`: U units whose outcome is `accepted` or `rejected` on originating or forwarded originating evidence

other: Three separate dimensions per unit: business outcome (`accepted`, `rejected`, `unresolved`, `conflicted`, `voided`), evidence basis (`originating_structured`, `forwarded_originating`, `record_specific_client_assertion`, `aggregate_only_assertion`, `no_usable_evidence`) and return expectation (`expected`, `structurally_unavailable`, `not_established`).

*1.0.1:* the evidence basis is the basis of the unit's **outcome** evidence: the final decision that supplies its outcome, or the assertion or aggregate note bound to it. Transport and syntax receipts without a final decision supply no outcome, so such a unit's basis is `no_usable_evidence`. The receipts themselves are accounted in M05.
`source_evidenced_outcomes` counts units with an originating or forwarded accepted **or rejected** outcome: supported rejection is outcome evidence. It is not an acceptance rate.
M16.title: Reporting disposition and outcome-evidence coverage

clauses.Clocks: *1.1.0* financial event `effective_at` <= T and `received_at` <= K; the window boundary (census `completed_at` + 336 h) against T; claim version `available_at` <= T for the constructed submitted charge; allocation rows qualifying at T and K
clauses.Denominator: *1.1.0* `<type>:expected_slots` for each slot type, and `settlements:count` for settlement allocation. Unlike types and currencies are never pooled
clauses.Exclusions: *1.1.0* none from F. Refund adjustments are source events, not expected slots (1.0.1), and are not in `settlements:*`; an event whose value is not known is not reconciled
clauses.Limits: *1.1.0* unknown is never zero. A settlement balances only when applied plus unapplied equals its signed amount in one currency with every applied target existing, and a zero residual does not prove completeness when source coverage is unknown
clauses.Lineage: *1.1.0* `src/cci/financial.py` (`facts`, `slots`, `reconcile`; `financial-slots.jsonl`, `allocation-reconciliation.json`) over F from `src/cci/expectations.py` `derive`, via `src/cci/cells.py`; slot policy `profiles.json` `financial_slot_policy`, meanings `financial-semantics.md`
clauses.Milestone: *1.1.0* service completion: initial slots are expected at completion and follow-up slots after the 336-hour observation window from completion; for P-C, the documented cancellation
clauses.Numerator: *1.1.0* not a single ratio: per slot type each state is a part of `<type>:expected_slots`; per settlement, applied plus unapplied amounts are compared with its signed amount
clauses.Population: *1.1.0* F (expected slots per completed leg and per P-C documented-cancelled request) and the settlement events known by K and effective by T

other: Per event type: expected slots and their states (`known`, `evidenced_derived_zero`, `unknown`, `not_yet_expected`, `not_applicable`, `conflicting`). After the 336-hour window a missing follow-up fact is `unknown`; the original source observation is retained beside it. Settlements: count, balanced, event total, allocated total and unapplied total in USD. No universal charge-minus-payment balance is claimed; unlike amounts are never pooled.
M17.title: Typed financial evidence and allocation

clauses.Clocks: *1.1.0* claim version `available_at` <= T; source and reference truth from rows received by K whose effect is by T
clauses.Denominator: *1.1.0* `versions`; at field grain, `fields_compared`. Each grain is partitioned into conforming, mismatch and unassessable
clauses.Exclusions: *1.1.0* versions that are not the latest of their family at T are outside the population; a version whose every source item has unknown census applicability is `unassessable`, not excluded
clauses.Grain: claim version (latest per family at T) and claim field
clauses.Limits: *1.1.0* a readiness result or receiver response does not prove this measure. While any version's active status is uncertain, the package contract withholds an unqualified overall rate
clauses.Milestone: *1.1.0* claim construction: the latest claim version per family available by T
clauses.Population: active constructed claim versions. A version conforms only when every required comparison is assessable and passes

clauses.Clocks: *1.1.0* unit `trigger_at`; the ready instant is the latest of the claim version's `available_at` and every supporting fact's `received_at` (and the P-B grouping window), at or before T and before the next version's `available_at`. A backdated `effective_at` cannot make readiness earlier
clauses.Denominator: *1.1.0* not a ratio: the stage's P units equal `ready` plus `never_ready_or_censored`
clauses.Exclusions: *1.1.0* none: units never ready by T, including units with no claim version and unassessable units, are counted in `never_ready_or_censored`
clauses.Grain: P unit per stage. Elapsed hours from the unit's governed trigger to the earliest established ready instant at that stage (*1.0.1, builder correction:* across the unit's claim versions, each counting only while it was the newest version; `first-ready.jsonl`) (the claim version and every supporting fact received by then). Never-ready and censored units sit beside the quantiles
clauses.Limits: *1.1.0* compare like triggers, targets and cohorts only. An authoritative retraction may invalidate historical readiness. Quantiles use the shared nearest-rank rule
clauses.Milestone: *1.1.0* from the governed preparation trigger (completion, or a P-C documented cancellation's `effective_at`) to the earliest established ready state at that stage
clauses.Numerator: *1.1.0* not a ratio: a duration distribution. `ready` counts units with an established ready instant; the quantiles are over their elapsed hours
clauses.Population: *1.1.0* P for that stage, the same units as the M15 `denominator`

C.members: completed legs whose census applicability is `reportable` and whose request is completed

C_unresolved.members: completed legs whose applicability is `unknown`, or whose request is not completed

F.members: expected financial slots per completed leg (supplier cost, submitted charge, then allowed amount, payer paid, member responsibility, member collection, vendor payment after the 336-hour window) and per P-C documented-cancelled request. *1.0.1:* refund adjustment is a source event type, not an expected slot (`profiles.json` `financial_slot_policy`)

P.members: one preparation unit per component per client target for every completed census leg (reportable or unresolved), plus one `cancelled_disposition` unit per target for every P-C documented-cancelled request

S.members: encounter families whose first business submission was made by T and is known by K

U.members: identical keys to P under this contract (one reporting unit per preparation unit)

shared_rules: Position Q(population version, T, K, rule version). Positions: `known_then` (T = K = 2026-07-14T23:59:59Z), `restated_then` (T = 2026-07-14T23:59:59Z, K = 2026-07-21T23:59:59Z), `current_later` (T = K = 2026-07-21T23:59:59Z). Population version `CCI-COHORT-1`; rule version `CCI-SYNTHETIC-CONTRACT-1/1.0.0`; definition version 1.0.0.
Availability. A row is available when `received_at <= K`; its business effect qualifies when `effective_at` is known and `<= T`. A null effective time never qualifies.

Counts are exact integers over identities at the declared grain. Rates are never stored: consumers compute numerator / denominator and round only for display. A zero denominator is undefined and displays `Not applicable`, never 0 percent. Client rates pool by summing numerators and denominators, never by averaging percentages.
Client filter: `ALL`; a profile (`P-A` = SYN-C01 and SYN-C02, `P-B` = SYN-C03 and SYN-C04, `P-C` = SYN-C05 and SYN-C06); or one client.

Period: `FULL` (service dates 2026-04-01 to 2026-06-29) or `SP1` (2026-04-01 to 2026-04-30), `SP2` (2026-05-01 to 2026-05-30), `SP3` (2026-05-31 to 2026-06-29). A record's period is its request's `service_date` (for a completed leg, the request named by its census row; for a claim version, its first source item). First-submission (S) measures M03, M05, M06, M11, M12 and M13 support `FULL` only: their cohort is the first-submission cohort and the service-date filter is never applied to it invisibly. M08 supports `ALL`/`FULL` only: unmatched and too-broad raw rows have no certain client binding.
Stage applies to M15 and M19 only: `initial_preparation`, `encounter_submission`, `audit_submission`. Everything else uses `-`.
Hours are elapsed hours rounded to 6 decimal places; medians and 90th percentiles use the nearest-rank method (k = ceil(q * n), the k-th smallest); empty populations give null.
Money is a decimal string with two places.

served_evidence.currency: historical: assembly-time validation receipt; the release-time validation bound to the release commit is governance/check-results.json and must carry the same status for every required check
historical: assembly-time diagnostics receipt (the diagnostics read the served bundle, so they run after assembly); governance/negative-controls.json must carry the same judgment for every instance
